findings.evidence: Ray.lean:102-122 is the file's whole public surface (grep of top-level declarations: `prodRayEquiv`, `coe_toCone_prodRayEquiv_symm_inl/inr` only). The cone-level model it mirrors supplies exactly these: `Algebraic/Ray/Basic.lean:425 prodSplit_eq_inl`, `:433 prodSplit_eq_inr`, with the docstring at `:391` noting "The two cases of the forward map are computed by ... prodSplit_eq_inl and ... prodSplit_eq_inr".
findings.fix: Add the forward characterization, e.g. `@[simp] theorem prodRayEquiv_eq_inl_iff (hΦ0 hΨ0) {ξ : (Φ.prod Ψ).Ray} {ρ : Φ.Ray} : Φ.prodRayEquiv Ψ hΦ0 hΨ0 ξ = .inl ρ ↔ ξ.toCone.1 = ρ.toCone.1.prod ⊥` and the `inr` counterpart (both directions hold, since `Fan.Ray` is determined by its cone).
findings.issue: `prodRayEquiv` is `(Equiv.ofBijective prodRayOfSum).symm`, so its forward map is `Function.surjInv` and no public lemma says what `Φ.prodRayEquiv Ψ hΦ0 hΨ0 ξ` is. Only the two `.symm` cone lemmas (lines 109, 117) exist. A consumer holding an arbitrary ray `ξ` of `Φ.prod Ψ` — the normal way boundary components of the product are indexed — cannot obtain the hypothesis `ξ.toCone.1 = ρ.toCone.1.prod ⊥` that the new boundary theorems require without re-deriving it through `Equiv.symm_apply_apply` plus `Subtype.ext`. The module docstring's claim that "a ray of the product projects to a ray of one factor and to the zero cone of the other" is stated by no public declaration.

findings.evidence: `Analytic/Fan/Boundary/Naturality.lean:62-66` `@[simp] FanEquiv.analyticMap_mem_analyticBoundaryComponent_iff` and `:74-78` `@[simp] preimage_analyticMap_analyticBoundaryComponent` are the same shape (mem-iff / preimage under the induced map) and are annotated; the distinguished-point lemma in this very file (line 46) is annotated, so the omission is inconsistent.
findings.fix: Mark both `@[simp]` (orientation is already the intrinsic one: push the homeomorph-side membership/preimage to the product-fan orbit). The boundary-file preimage lemmas should stay non-simp, since `ξ` there is not determined by the LHS.
findings.issue: `analyticProdHomeomorph_mem_prod_analyticConeOrbit_iff` (line 58) and `preimage_analyticProdHomeomorph_prod_analyticConeOrbit` (line 81) carry no `@[simp]`, although every variable on the RHS already occurs on the LHS and the identically-shaped naturality lemmas on `main` are simp.

summary: The exposed surface is minimal and the `.symm` direction of `prodRayEquiv` is fully characterized, but the forward direction of the equiv (defined via `surjInv`, hence opaque) has no characterizing lemma, unlike its cone-level model `ToricRay.prodSplit`. The two product-orbit lemmas also lack the `@[simp]` their in-repo analogues carry.
